newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - FEB 4.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - FEB 4.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said he insisted on adding a second tier to Hungary's 'pay as you go' pension system, although the government plans were controversial.
- The Chairman of the state privatisation agency APV said that state monopoly in the electricity sector should not be replaced by private monopoly.
- An opposition MP said at the session of the parliament that the government would be able to cut motorway tolls by 30 percent by using VAT on the tolls for that purpose.
- The local municipality found temporary accommodation for several Budapest citizens whose flats were damaged by an explosion on Monday.
- The state should help each children to be brought up in a family, the draft child protection law, submitted to parliament on Tuesday says.
